hook.say: Ninety-nine percent of people don't know what C-D-A means.

decides.say: But if you ride a bike, it decides how fast you go.
chunks: But if you ride a bike,

air.say: At race speed, about eighty-five percent of your effort goes into one thing: pushing air out of the way.

blunt.say: Air has to flow around you. A blunt shape tears the flow apart, and leaves a messy, swirling wake behind it. That wake is drag.

smooth.say: A smooth shape lets the air close back in. Same width, about ten times less drag.

cd.say: That slipperiness has a name: C-D, the drag coefficient.

area.say: The second part is A, your frontal area. How big you look to the wind.

cda.say: Multiply them, and you get C-D-A. One number for how hard the air pushes back.

speed.say: Same rider, same two hundred fifty watts. Lower C-D-A: two kilometers per hour faster. Three and a half minutes over forty kilometers.

tuck.say: Lower your back. Narrow your elbows. Tuck your head. Small changes, free speed.
